title: 3.8.18 Lab: Save a State Object by Key
description: Turn a state object into JSON text and store it under a key, the way a page would keep it between visits. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the state object
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it state; use any name that fits) holding an object with at least two properties, for example a score and a level.

steps.title: Store it under a key
steps.instructions: Use localStorage.setItem to save the object under a key you choose. Remember the store holds strings, so the object has to be converted with JSON.stringify first.

steps.title: Read the key back
steps.instructions: Use console.log with localStorage.getItem on the same key to confirm text was stored.

requirements.title: State object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: Declare an object (the lesson calls it state) with at least two properties.

requirements.title: Stored by key
requirements.hint: localStorage.setItem takes two things: a key name and the text to store under it.

requirements.title: Converted with stringify
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify before storing. Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: The store only holds text, so turn the object into text with JSON.stringify before you pass it in.

requirements.title: Key read back
requirements.hint: Read it back with localStorage.getItem, using the same key you saved under.

requirements.title: Stored text logged
requirements.hint: Wrap the getItem call in console.log so the stored text is printed.

requirements.title: the stored text is state turned into JSON and it is printed back
requirements.description: The text printed from localStorage.getItem is the JSON text of state (written on one line or spread over several). Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: Store JSON.stringify(state) under a key, then print localStorage.getItem with that same key. Storing the object itself or other text would not match state.

NEAR(x, y) : JSON.stringify(x) === JSON.stringify(y); const SAMEA = (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b) && a.length === b.length && a.every((x, i) => SAMEV(x, b[i])); const CONTIG = (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b) && a.length > 0 && a.length <= b.length && b.some((_, at) => at + a.length <= b.length && a.every((x, i) => SAMEV(x, b[at + i]))); const JEQ = (a, b) => JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b); const PRINTS = (J, vs) => vs.every((x) => typeof x === 'number' ? Object.values(v).reduce((a, x) => a.concat(LEAVES(x)), []) : [v]; const JSONS = (t) => { const found = []; const txt = String(t).slice(0, 20000); for (let i = 0; i < txt.length && found.length < 40; i++) { if (txt[i] !== '{' && txt[i] !== '[') continue; let d = 0; let q = false; for (let j = i; j < txt.length; j++) { const ch = txt[j]; if (q) { if (ch === '\\') j++; else if (ch === '"') q = false; continue; } if (ch === '"') q = true; else if (ch === '{' || ch === '[') d++; else if (ch === '}' || ch === ']') { d--; if (d === 0) { try { found.push(JSON.parse(txt.slice(i, j + 1))); } catch (e) { } break; } } } } return found; }; return (state !== null && typeof state === 'object' && Object.keys(state).length >= 2 && JSONS(output.join('\n')).some(($o) => JEQ($o, state)) && (() => { for (let $i = 0; $i < localStorage.length; $i++) { try { if (JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(localStorage.key($i)))) === JSON.stringify(state)) return true; } catch (e) { } } return false; })()); })()

requirements.title: what getItem reads back is printed, by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints what localStorage.getItem reads back, and that text changes when state does. Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: Print the getItem call itself: console.log(localStorage.getItem("yourKey")). Printing JSON.stringify(state) directly, or typed-in text, does not show what was stored.
